reviews.decision_reason: Synthesis applies the explicit eight-item window and derives the recommendation from the first priority record; the observed final output is consistent with that role. It does not independently establish demand quality, but it is not the source of the unsupported demand claims.

Coverage mapping retains only allowed record identifiers and maps exact need text to the supplied capabilities. Unsupported records n06-r01 and n06-r07 reflect missing matching capabilities, not a mapping defect.

Prioritization ranks unsupported needs before covered needs and orders by upstream provenance rank within each group, producing the observed top unsupported need. The behavior matches the declared downstream contract.

Demand selection is the top root cause. It accepts all rows with demand_score >= 3, plus fallback records, as demand-bearing even though the supplied corpus only contains asserted internal needs and scores. The package shows no observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes supporting those market-demand claims, so the downstream recommendation is built on unsupported demand evidence.

Evidence normalization preserves and bounds the selected rows, but it also carries forward demand records without adding or checking the market-demand support required by the review criteria. This is downstream of the selection fault rather than the clearest root cause.

Provenance assembly ranks normalized need records by asserted demand_score and assembles source handoff records, but the source records are only ids and weights. They do not expose observed jobs, pain, triggers, alternatives, consequences, or outcomes, so provenance rank should not be treated as validated market demand. This is propagation of the upstream selection defect.
